title: MI5 says over 100 UK academics worked on projects funded by China’s spies
summary:
MI5 has told UK universities to review any work with the China General Technology Research Institute (CGTRI).
More than 100 UK-linked academics have worked on its projects, according to MI5.
AI, cybersecurity and steganographyUK academics have contributed to CGTRI-funded projects on AI, cybersecurity, covert communications systems and steganography, according to MI5.
“This alert exposes attempts by Chinese intelligence to covertly benefit from the expertise and research of our academics,” Jarvis said.
China rejects the claims“The accusations made by the UK intelligence agency against the relevant Chinese entity are imaginary and purely fabricated,” the Chinese embassy in London said.

title: Putin shows no sign of stopping the war as Russia doubles down on Ukraine
summary:
When Vladimir Putin arrived to address Russia's parliament on Wednesday, a warm welcome was guaranteed.
"The Special Election Operation", as one Russian newspaper dubbed last month's legislative vote, has produced a State Duma even more pro-Putin than anything before it.
Are there any signs he is prepared to halt what he calls the special military operation?
Right now, everything points to Putin continuing Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine: despite his country's huge battlefield losses to date and the damage being done to Russia's economy.
Putin's speeches and statements suggest he remains confident that Russia can secure a military victory.

title: An American Journalist Imprisoned as a Spy in Russia
summary:
Listen and subscribe: Apple | Spotify | Wherever You ListenSign up for our daily newsletter to get the best of The New Yorker in your inbox.
In 2023, Evan Gershkovich was working as a young reporter in Moscow for the Wall Street Journal, when he was arrested by Russian authorities.
He was eventually convicted on blatantly false charges of espionage and spent nearly five hundred days in imprisonment.
Gershkovich recounts the experience in a new memoir, “This Cursed Beautiful Land,” and in an essay in The New Yorker.
He spoke with David Remnick about life inside a Russian prison, the international prisoner swap that freed him, and why the difficult process of reacclimating to his former life complicated how he viewed his incarceration.

title: Morocco’s pro-Palestine protests challenge Rabat’s deepening Israel ties
summary:
Protests across Morocco highlight gap between public opposition to normalisation and Rabat’s closer ties with Israel.
Pro-Palestine protests have spread across several Moroccan cities, with demonstrators demanding an end to diplomatic normalisation with Israel as Rabat deepens ties with Tel Aviv.
The move therefore goes beyond maintaining diplomatic relations established in 2020.
Public opinion and state policyMorocco has maintained diplomatic relations with Israel while continuing to publicly support the Palestinian cause and the establishment of a Palestinian state.
Whether that public opposition translates into sustained political pressure remains less clear.
